title: Why only one group of Americans is increasingly likely to have a third child | Institute for Family Studies
gist: Teaser of a Washington Post piece (Shannon Osaka): the long-standing inverse relationship between income and family size is reversing, with wealthier U.S. families now having more children than middle-class ones, and a third child may be becoming more than a wealth marker.

insights.claim: For decades the accepted pattern was that higher family income meant fewer children.
insights.speaker: Shannon Osaka
insights.so_what: Baseline assumption in demographic models that is now being questioned.
insights.quote: The higher the family income, the fewer children you have.

insights.claim: In recent years the income-fertility relationship has started to reverse, with wealthier families beginning to have more children than middle-class families.
insights.speaker: Shannon Osaka
insights.so_what: Children becoming a luxury good shifts where family-related consumer demand concentrates (high-income households) and highlights middle-class affordability squeezes.

insights.speaker: Shannon Osaka
